big-news.text: Norway beat Wales 3–1 at Ullevaal, with goals from Nusa, Schjelderup and a late Haaland penalty. That locks in a top seed for the Euro 2028 qualifying draw. Next up is Denmark in Copenhagen on Tuesday.
Bird flu has been found on a farm in Akershus, so 13,000 laying hens must be culled and there's a 3 km protection zone. Mattilsynet, the food safety authority, says it's no risk to food safety.
UK prosecutors won't appeal the 20-year sentence given to a Norwegian 19-year-old for conspiracy to murder. He won't appeal either and will apply to serve it in Norway.

oslo.text: Oslo Venstre picked Hallstein Bjercke and Marit Vea to top its list for next year's local election. Several candidates with minority backgrounds dropped out in protest over the list.

be-aware.text: There's a yellow gale warning on the outer Oslofjord coast until about 17:00, plus heavy drifting snow in parts of the southern mountains this morning.

fun-and-free.text: Top pick: The Frank Znort Quartet plays a free concert at Blå at 16:30, a classic Sunday jazz hang by the Akerselva.
Jul i Vinterland at Spikersuppa is open 10:00–20:00, with stalls, free concerts and a Ferris wheel.
It's the last day of the Kunstbok Oslo art book fair at the National Library, 11:00–18:00, with free entry.
Sentralen has Icelandic choirs and Greenlandic drum dancing at 12:00, and Deichman Bjørvika has a family concert at 13:00. Both are free.
There are school flea markets at Høyenhall (10:00) and Årvoll (11:00), plus the Birkelunden market from 12:00.
Today is your last chance for "Sprayboksen 100 år" at Teknisk Museum. It's ticketed, not free.
